newsitem.title: USA: Tuberculosis found in Hawaiian cattle herd - USDA.
newsitem.headline: Tuberculosis found in Hawaiian cattle herd - USDA.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Department said Friday tuberculosis was found in a cattle herd in Hawaii, and that the state no longer meets the criteria for designation as an accredited-free tuberculosis state.
In a Federal Register notice, the USDA said it changed Hawaii's designation to "accredited-free (suspended)."

Hawaii will be eligible to apply for accredited-free designation after an epidemiological investigation confirms that the disease has not spread from the infected herd and all cattle and bison involved were destroyed, the USDA said.
The USDA said tuberculosis was confirmed in one cattle herd on the island of Molokai.
In 1992, Hawaii had 874 cattle herds containing 191,230 cattle, with the majority of herds owned by small businesses.

"Changing the status of Hawaii may affect the marketability of cattle from the state, since some prospective cattle buyers prefer to buy cattle from accredited-free states," USDA said in the notice. "This may result in a small detrimental economic impact on some small entities, although it appears that sales of cattle from Hawaii to other states are quite small in volume."
